name: Light
summary: Across creation, Light flows through living things, and its power is called upon in Azeroth as Holy magic. Faith and will can turn it to healing, shelter, or a strike against darkness.

sections.title: A Primal Force
sections.body: Across creation, Light flows as living energy. In Azeroth, it takes the form of Holy magic, moving through living souls and binding mortal hearts. Mortals may picture it as a conscious protector. Yet Light answers the absolute conviction of the soul that calls upon it.

sections.title: Instruments of Faith
sections.body: Channeling Light calls for self-abnegation, disciplined meditation, and unshakable will. Priests of the Church of the Holy Light and holy paladins train for years to become clear vessels for its radiance. Through devotion, Light can mend wounds with restorative warmth and shelter the innocent with brilliant wards. It can also strike demons and the risen undead with searing fire.

sections.title: Many Faces of Radiance
sections.body: Humans and dwarves revere Light through formal scripture, while other peoples follow their own spiritual traditions. Night elves devote themselves to Elune and channel sacred moonlight, weaving holy magic to cleanse and protect. Tauren honor the sun deity An'she through their own spiritual traditions.

faq.answer: Light is a fundamental cosmic energy found across creation. As a primal source of life and positive energy, it binds sentient souls together. Mortals call upon it for Holy magic that heals, protects, and aids them in warfare.

faq.q: Does the Light have a conscious will or mind?
faq.answer: Light is a primal cosmic force rather than a god. Mortals may speak of its will and treat it as a guiding patron, but it does not share mortal morality. It answers the caster's certainty, willpower, and faith.

faq.q: Why can evil zealots still use the Light?
aliases: why do scarlet crusade have light
can bad guys use the light
faq.answer: Light answers conviction, not abstract righteousness. If a caster has absolute faith that their cause is just and an undivided spirit, Light can flow through them, even when their deeds are ruthless or misguided.

faq.q: How does the Light affect the undead?
faq.answer: Holy magic is a powerful weapon against the Scourge, yet it can also heal undead bodies. Channeling Light or receiving its healing brings intense pain to the undead, but does not automatically burn away their flesh.

faq.q: How do priests and paladins learn to wield it?
faq.answer: Wielding Light takes rigorous mental discipline, emotional clarity, and years of meditation. A caster must quiet personal ego and focus their spirit entirely, becoming a clear conduit through which Holy magic pours into the world.

faq.q: Is Elune's magic connected to the Light?
faq.answer: Yes. The moonlight channeled by Elune's priestesses appears as holy magic. It can restore, protect, and purify, like the spells wielded by paladins and church priests.

angles.text: As a paladin, you join martial discipline and your mortal body with Light. You wield its incandescent fury against the Scourge and demonic evil.
As a priest, you serve as a spiritual shepherd and conduit. Through deep meditation and prayer, you mend flesh, steady broken spirits, and shield allies.
As an Alliance member, you find Stormwind and Ironforge's spiritual bedrock in the Church of the Holy Light. It offers hope in an era darkened by Lordaeron's fall.
As Forsaken, channeling Light or receiving its healing brings you intense pain, even when the spell mends your body.
As a night elf, you channel holy energy through reverence for the moon goddess Elune and her silver light, rather than church doctrine.
As a tauren, you revere An'she, the golden right eye of the Earth Mother, through traditional sun worship.
